title: terraform: refactor private deployment state layout + modularize GPU node pools, IAM & networking
author: Aisha Bennett
description:
Context: Private deployments require clearer separation of Terraform state and smaller, reusable modules for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking to support multi-environment upgrades, easier rollback, and clearer ownership. Motivation: recent on-prem upgrades surfaced long plan/apply times and risky global state changes when introducing new node pool types and IAM bindings. This PR refactors the state layout and extracts three primary modules to reduce blast radius and make upgrades deterministic.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduces modules/gpu_node_pool, modules/iam_roles, and modules/networking with clear inputs/outputs and example usages.
- Moves from a single monolithic "private-cluster" state to per-concern state files: networking.tfstate, iam.tfstate, compute-gpu-<env>.tfstate.
- Adds state migration scripts (scripts/migrate_state.sh) to copy and lock legacy state to the new buckets with idempotency checks.
- Adds an upgrade helper (scripts/upgrade_private_deploy.sh) that applies in order: networking -> iam -> gpu node pools, with an automated retry backoff and canary annotation support.
- Adds rollback hooks (scripts/rollback_partial.sh) to tear down a newly created node pool if health checks fail during rollout.
- Adds unit and integration examples in examples/private/gpu (including a small cluster with a single A10G pool) and updates READMEs.
- Updates documentation in docs/private/state-layout.md and an upgrade runbook (docs/private/upgrade-runbook.md).

Checklist: 
- [x] Create reusable modules for GPU node pools, IAM roles/policies and networking.
- [x] Implement per-concern remote state layout and backend configuration.
- [x] Provide state migration tooling and dry-run support.
- [x] Add upgrade/rollback helper scripts and runbook.
- [x] Update examples and docs.
- [x] Add CI checks for `terraform fmt`, `tflint`, and `terraform validate` on modules.

Compatibility notes:
- No change to the public API of the installer. Existing customers must run scripts/migrate_state.sh to migrate state to the new layout. The migration script performs a dry-run and requires a confirmation flag to proceed.

Testing performed:
- Local integration runs against a test GCP project with a small cluster and simulated network.
- Ran migration dry-run on a snapshot of production state and verified plan diffs are limited to backend config updates.
- CI added module-level validate steps that ran on PR and passed.

Related: Linear ENG-8743 tracks the follow-up automation to add canary rollout flags to the console; SUP-4321 is a customer ticket that motivated the state refactor.

Notes for reviewers: focus review on module interfaces and state migration safety checks. The scripts include conservative checks (state locks, bucket write verification, plan cache) but please call out additional failure modes you expect in on-prem environments.

merge_outcome: Merged by Gregor Chen via squash and merge on 2026-02-20. Merge commit message: 'refactor(private): modularize state + gpu/iam/networking modules, add migration & upgrade tooling (ENG-8743)'.
release_notes: Refactor: modularized Terraform for Private deployments (GPU node pools, IAM, networking). Added state migration tooling and upgrade/rollback helpers. Customers must run scripts/migrate_state.sh as part of upgrade. See docs/private/state-layout.md and docs/private/upgrade-runbook.md for migration instructions.
notes_for_ops: Before upgrading a production private deployment: 1) run scripts/migrate_state.sh --dry-run and review plan; 2) ensure service account used for migration has bucket write/list/locking permissions; 3) follow runbook to apply networking -> iam -> compute in that order; 4) monitor canary pool health for at least 10 minutes before full rollout.
security_considerations: IAM module introduces least-privilege role creation for nodepool ops; review required for legacy service-account bindings. Migration keeps existing bindings by default but flags any widened roles in the migration plan.
